content:
maggie (Marketing): Kicking off the Zenith Systems customer story — they flagged the high-level narrative as good but we still need a final quote + legal OK. Who can own the 30min interview and harvest a quote this week?

sam (Content): I can take the interview. Prefer Wed morning — need a short brief and 6-8 seed questions. Also a suggested quote to send for approval.

jordan (Product): I'll draft the technical Qs. Must capture Dedicated deployment details, p95 latency improvements, and perceived infra simplification.

maggie (Marketing): Diego, can you re-introduce our comms lead to the Zenith PM so Sam can schedule?

diego (Sales): On it. Just re-introduced and dropped a Doodle for Wed/Thu. Proposed quote we had earlier below — feel free to soften: "With Redwood Dedicated, we cut inference costs by ~45% and p95 latency dropped by half, letting us double throughput without infra changes."

linda (Legal): Legal checklist: (1) No public attribution without explicit written approval, (2) No publishing of confidential internal metrics or dollar amounts, (3) If they request anonymity, we need an NDA addendum. Please send a one-line approval box in the email.

sam (Content): Draft email to Zenith (copy):
```
Hi <Name>,

Thanks for agreeing to the case study. Below is the proposed quote we plan to publish. Reply with edits or "Approved" and we'll proceed.

Proposed quote: "Redwood Dedicated significantly reduced our inference costs and improved p95 latency, enabling higher throughput during peak usage."

If you're comfortable, please reply: "I approve the quote above for public use by Redwood Inference." 

Thanks,
Sam
```

maggie (Marketing): Linda — any preferred legal phrasing we should include so approvals are audit-ready? :lock:

linda (Legal): Add exactly that approval sentence for auditability. Remove percentage numbers unless the customer explicitly wants them in writing. If they want anonymity, use "a leading fintech company" and route them to an NDA.

jordan (Product): For accuracy, prefer we say "p95 latency" rather than "tail latency". Also only add infra tags like "on our amp deployment" if they confirm the environment.

sam (Content): I'll send the email in ~30m after rewording. Will ping when sent.

diego (Sales): Zenith responded — can do Thu 10am PT. They asked to soften the numeric claims; I've suggested the non-numeric line above and told them we'll wait for their confirmation.

maggie (Marketing): Once they sign off we need ops to add inbound lead routing from the case-study page to SDR queue and tag the CRM record with case-study metadata. ops-bot, can you paste the routing snippet?

ops-bot: Proposed routing rule for ops team:
```
route: /case-studies/zenith -> sales.sdr.queue
add_tag: crm.account.tags += ["case-study:zenith"]
notify: #sales-inbound (webhook)
```

ops-bot: Also setting demo request TTL from that page to 90 days.

linda (Legal): After they approve, ask them to send a one-line approval email we can store. Legal will keep the signed copy for audit.

sam (Content): Sent. Included the approval sentence. Pinged here with the outbound email and schedule.

maggie (Marketing): Thanks. Next steps: Sam — run interview + collect final approved quote; Jordan — validate tech phrasing post-interview; Linda — confirm legal copy in our asset folder; Diego — confirm co-marketing lead permissions; Ops — implement routing + tags when we publish. Plan a fast design pass for the case layout and write a short benchmark blurb to slot into the launch post.

diego (Sales): Will flag co-marketing leads as "co-marketing:zenith" in CRM only after we get explicit permission from Zenith.

maggie (Marketing): Great. We'll aim to publish the case story + a short webinar invite to targeted accounts two weeks after approval. Meeting recap: Sam = interview + quote send, Jordan = tech accuracy, Linda = legal sign-off and audit copy, Diego = customer comms + lead gating, Maggie = launch owner. Reopen thread when quote is approved. :thumbsup:
